newsitem.title: UK: Dollar/mark steady in Europe, holds above 1.72.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/mark steady in Europe, holds above 1.72.

text.p: The dollar jogged in place around 1.7250 marks at midday in Europe, uncertain about its next step after a Bundesbank council member said he wouldn't rule out another cut in rates and also warned of an EMU delay.

His comments cancelled each other out and gave little fresh direction to dollar/mark, said analysts, adding that while a cut in German rates would weigh on the mark, a delay to European monetary union would boost it.
"The European markets have looked to the whole set of comments," said Hans-Guenter Redeker, analyst at Chase Investment Bank.
Redeker said a German rate cut would depress the mark but a delay to European monetary union would boost it.

At 0945 GMT, dollar/mark stood at 1.7254/56 against 1.7252/62 marks in late Europe and well off highs of 1.7281 marks hit in Asia. Dollar/yen was also steady to a touch softer, trading at 113.75/3.80 against 113.98/08 in late Europe.

The dollar was hoisted to highs above 1.780 marks in Asia after Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said he wouldn't rule out another cut in rates. But drifted off overnight highs in Europe as markets digested a raft of Jochimsen comments, said analysts.

"It is the first comment we have had from a Bundesbank official for some time suggesting there is still scope for rate cuts and holding out the prospect of further Bundesbank easing," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.

But, he added, Jochimsen's comment was blunted by the fact that while saying he did not rule out another cut in rates, he also said he did not see one. "He didn't really, give the market too much of a clue," said Stamenkovic.
Jochimsen said he would not rule out another cut in Bundesbank rates in the present economic cycle but also added that he did not see one.
Analysts said overall, however, his comments had failed to give clear direction to the dollar as it now seemed undecided about which way it wanted to trade.

The market also got mixed signals from the Bundesbank's Jochimsen on European monetary union. Jochimsen warned the prospects for EMU were being threatened by the lack of political integration and by a fundamental dissent between Germany and France. Comments like this, said traders, would normally be mark supportive.
But some were also confused as Jochimsen said a postponement to EMU would not necessarily lead to mark appreciation.
"Jochimsen, was also talking about the riks of the EMU process, putting alot of emphasis on the situation in France and that is one of the market focuses in the next two months," said Redeker.
Jochimsen warned on Wednesday prospects for EMU were being threatened by a lack of political integration and by a fundamental dissent between France and Germany.

He warned that France and Germany urgently needed to resolve fundamental differences regarding French calls for a political counterweight to the European Central Bank and for EU-wide policies to create jobs.
With the dollar rangebound at midday in Europe, analysts said it should get clear direction once the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is over on July 1-2.
While analysts expect rates to remain unchanged after the next meeting, traders will nevertheless remain cautious in the run-up to it.

"The only thing that will give clear direction to the dollar will be interest-rate expectations once the FOMC meeting is out of the way," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch.

Elsewhere, the Bundesbank was meeting for a regular policy-making meeting but economists are convinced it will keep rates unchanged. The Buba said it would not hold a news conference after its meeting.

The mark was steady to slightly firmer on its crosses, recovering slightly against the lira after mark/lira slipped to near five-month lows around 975.00 on Wednesday. At midday in Europe it was trading at 976.50 lire.
--Julia Meehan, London newsroom +4471 542 6701
